caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:000045
attempts.entry_title: Standardized and reproducible decision-making in mice (The International Brain Laboratory 2021)
attempts.summary: The paper's main findings on consistency across laboratories largely held: mice in seven labs performed alike at proficiency, a classifier could not identify the lab, and mice used block priors in the full task. Learning speed was partly matched, with labs differing in days to proficiency but more weakly than reported. Only 83 mice reached basic proficiency against 140, because the dataset lacks mice trained before June 2019. Predicting slow learners from early sessions could not be tested, as the paper does not describe the method. Some secondary lab comparisons in the full task did not hold.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of The International Brain Laboratory (2021) on dandiset 000045, which holds the trial tables of 178 mice trained in seven laboratories from June 2019 to March 2020. It recomputes basic and full task proficiency from the trials and compares training times, psychometric parameters, block effects, the choice model and session ends with the paper, across laboratories. The dandiset holds no sessions before June 2019 and no training status.

notebooks.title: Reproducing The International Brain Laboratory (2021) from dandiset 000045

outcomes.notes: The dataset holds 177 mice of the paper's project; 136 have their whole training in it (first session a first-stage session), against 206 that started training. Under the main reading 83 reach basic task proficiency (61 first with status 1a, 22 with 1b), against 140; the pipeline's contrast check gives 85, and 1b replacing 1a from 2019-09-12 gives 70 and 71. 60 reach full task proficiency, against 98. No count is within tolerance under any reading. The answers of 2026-10-22 changed P1 (each session and the two before it, any protocol; all trials counted; percent correct over 50% and 100% contrasts; 1a or 1b at any date), which moved the count from 75 to 84 under the earlier readings to 83 under the main one; the outcome is the same as before (not_reproduced). The dataset holds sessions from 2019-06-11 to 2020-03-23; the Methods say training of these mice began in January 2019. No window fails the 1b or P2 criteria only because missing stimulus onsets leave its reaction time undefined (0 windows under every reading), so the missing onsets do not lower the counts. P2 slides over full-task days; 10 days with more than one full-task session fall at or before a mouse's P2 day, or on any day of a mouse without P2, in 7 mice, so a count over sessions could differ for at most 7 mice.
deviations: Proficiency is recomputed from the trials, as the files carry no training status.
P2 is computed over three consecutive full-task days, not sessions (see notes).
Mice whose first session in the dataset is not a first-stage session (41) are left out, as their training began before the dataset does.

outcomes.notes: Under the main reading (83 mice) the mean days to P1 is 19.87 counting the P1 day and 18.87 without, both within 18.4 +- 1.84, and the slowest mouse takes 58 and 57 days, within 59 +- 5.9. The s.d. is 11.39 (against 13.0 +- 1.3) and the fastest mouse takes 5 or 4 days (against 3 +- 0.3); two of four values are within tolerance. The variants give means of 17.73 to 23.17 days and at most two values within tolerance. Six of the 136 whole-training mice have their first session in the dataset's first 7 days, where an earlier start would go unseen; without the 2 of them that reach P1 the mean is 19.40 days (s.d. 10.98, fastest 5, slowest 58), again two of four within tolerance. The five fastest mice start between 2019-08-06 and 2019-11-21. The answers changed P1 (see cohort-counts); the outcome is the same as before (partially_reproduced). Measured is the main reading, counting the P1 day.
deviations: 83 mice, against 140.

outcomes.notes: Kruskal-Wallis across labs p = 0.029 under the main reading (0.023 to 0.088 under the variants), never below 0.001; the code's switch gives the same tests. Lab 2 interquartile range 7.75 days (within 8 +- 0.8), Lab 6 5.75 days (against 22 +- 2.2). The labs differ at p < 0.05 but not at the p < 0.001 the criterion requires, and one of the two ranges matches, so the effect is present but weaker. Changed from not_reproduced after the verifier's round 1, which gave partially_reproduced for this reason.
deviations: 6 to 26 mice per lab.

outcomes.notes: Under the main reading the mean trials to P1 is 11,839 counting the P1 day and 11,104 without, within 10,800 +- 1,080; the s.d. (7,515 and 7,472), fastest (2,357 and 1,687) and slowest (34,998 and 34,265) are outside tolerance. The mean cumulative trials when mean easy-trial performance first exceeds 80% is 7,329 (within 7,400 +- 740), and 6,659 to 7,306 under the variants. The answers changed P1; the outcome is the same as before (partially_reproduced).
deviations: The median filter over 3 sessions is pandas' centred rolling median with partial windows at the ends, a standard choice; the claims file does not fix the edges.

outcomes.notes: Over the 136 mice that started training in the dataset, mice without P1 censored, the Kaplan-Meier proportion at day 40 is 0.749 counting the P1 day and 0.749 without under the main reading, within 0.8 +- 0.08, and 1.000 at the last day. Since round 1 a mouse without P1 is censored at its last training day counted the same way as the events (before, at the count including the P1 day under both counts), which moved the count without the P1 day from 0.741 to 0.749. The pipeline's contrast check, a variant, gives 0.768; 1b replacing 1a from 2019-09-12 gives 0.600 to 0.602, outside tolerance. The code's variant, leaving out mice still in training at the cutoff, gives 0.815 under the main reading. The answer to the question on "all contrasts introduced" (each of the three sessions, the main reading; the pipeline's check of the current session a variant; pooling given by neither) settled the reading that blocked the claim, and the change of P1 to the pipeline's computation moved the proportion under that reading from 0.670 to 0.678 to 0.741 to 0.749. Earlier outcome blocked (methods_underspecified).

outcomes.notes: Under every reading the threshold interquartile range narrows after day 10 (main, filtered, days 10 to 39, 11.5-23.7% against 11.1-24.3%), but no reading puts all eight bounds within tolerance; the main reading puts at most four (filtered, days 10 on). outcomes.notes: The project mice have 6,539 sessions (against 10,903). 5,698 met an end criterion and 841 ended earlier (13%, against 5,316 of 10,903, 49%). Extra trials median 16.0, m.a.d. 14.0, against 19 +- 1.9 and 16 +- 1.6. Only the count of sessions meeting a criterion is within tolerance, while the share differs. Per training day, counting a day as met when a session met a criterion or the day's sessions lasted 90 minutes or more, 5,683 of 6,435 days met one. The criterion defines the count per training day, but the outcome is decided on the per-session count; the outcome is the same either way. Recomputing the criteria also for the 722 sessions whose status is False, a variant, gives 5,734 of 6,539 (88%), with the same extra trials. Not affected by the answers.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds 178 mice and 6,615 sessions from 2019-06-11 to 2020-03-23. The paper's mice began training in January 2019 (206 mice, 10,903 sessions), so 41 mice of the project begin mid-training in the dandiset and the mice trained before June 2019 are missing.

The training status of each session (in_training, trained_1a, trained_1b, ready4ephysrig and so on), on which every analysis of the paper selects sessions, is not in the files. It has to be recomputed from the trials, which leaves open details of the criteria.
One recording is deposited twice, under two mice (CSHL_013 and CSHL_015, 2019-07-15, identical trials and start time).

probabilityLeft is described as the probability of a left stimulus for the current block, but in every basic-task session it varies from trial to trial between 0 and 1 (24% of basic-task trials are not 0.5), with the stimulus side following it.
session_start_time is stated in UTC (+00:00) but holds local clock times; all seven labs, from London to Berkeley, have median start hours between 11.0 and 14.4 h.

In 807 files the wheel position data and its timestamps differ in length (for example 181,623 samples against 340,799 timestamps); 16 files have no wheel series. In one session checked (ibl_witten_07), the wheel moves the opposite way to the choice on every trial.

257,021 trials (6%) have no stimulus onset time, and 185 sessions have none; 1,541 trials in 220 sessions have a response time before the stimulus onset (down to -5,638 s). No proficiency window of this attempt fails for the missing onsets alone.
One session (ZM_1367, 2019-06-11) uses contrasts of 4% and 8%, which the paper does not describe.

The Methods give the 1a/1b performance criterion on easy trials and the Results give the lapse criterion as a maximum of 0.2 for the sum of the lapses, while Appendix 1, table 1d gives performance on 100% contrast and a bound on each lapse rate. After the answers of 2026-10-22 the claims file follows the pipeline's code for performance (easy trials) and the table for the lapses; with performance on 100% contrast only, 84 mice reach P1 against 83.
The dandiset's metadata do not say which of its 178 mice are the paper's; one mouse (SWC_029) belongs to another project by its subject record.

verifications.reviewed: The executed notebook of the run after the answers of 2026-10-22 (commit 64c34593), with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module, the claims file and the paper. The verifier tested helper functions on synthetic inputs and checked the archive's versions and file lists. Report in transcripts/000045/verifier-1-report.md. The cell numbers in the reasons below refer to that notebook, not to the current one.

disagreements.reason: Cell 16: Kruskal-Wallis p=0.029, so the labs differ at 0.05 but not at the required <0.001. Lab 2 IQR 7.75 is in tolerance; Lab 6 IQR 5.75 is far from 22.
Cell 39: s.d. 219 ms is in tolerance. Median 420.4 ms is just outside (needs >= 421.2). Lab p=0.061 uncorrected, so the lab difference is not shown.

Cell 73: Logistic Regression is not above chance (2.5th percentile 0.000 vs 0.070). Cell 75: Random Forest ran only 6 of the 2000 subsamples; those 6 are not above chance, but that decides nothing. It also noted (problem 4) that the Random Forest needs about 4.9 h single-threaded on data already loaded, a block that is not a data limit, and asked for the full 2000-subsample run in parallel.
Cell 51: 91 mice vs 150+-15. Trials per session differs (FDR p=0.002) as claimed, but trials per minute also differs (FDR p=0.002). Cell 73: the classifier is not above chance.
Cell 82: the rewarded test passes under every reading (t about 9.9). The unrewarded test passes with the code's sessions (t=3.54, p=7e-4) but fails with reading (b) (p=0.30).

Cell 84: accuracy (81.9 / 83.5) and full-model condition number 3.14 are in tolerance under every reading. Basic condition number is 2.38 under the code's model (no 50% trials), which reproduces as fig5cf's under-one-reading rule allows. entries.title: Standardized and reproducible decision-making in mice (The International Brain Laboratory 2021)
entries.description: Tests the findings of The International Brain Laboratory (2021) on dandiset 000045, which holds the trial tables of 178 mice trained in seven laboratories from June 2019 to March 2020. It recomputes basic and full task proficiency from the trials and compares training times, psychometric parameters, block effects, the choice model and session ends with the paper, across laboratories. The dandiset holds no sessions before June 2019 and no training status.
